reviews.title: Glitchy
reviews.text:
I spent a lot of money on this app. Always freezes, lags, stops working. Closes randomly. If you type a word incorrectly by missing just one letter, it is unable to guess what the correct word is and shows no results. Constantly reminds me that I can put an asterisk if I know how to spell something. As an example of its stupidity, when I type in “adumbration,” it shows no results although that is an entry under “adumbrate.” 

Clearly designed by people who never even use it. What a waste. Previous, simpler versions were way better. By trying to add features and redesign it, the developers have ruined what was a very helpful app. Used to be an affordable monthly subscription, but then the price became so ridiculous that an annual subscription was the only reasonable option. I did not even get through half a year this app is so abysmal.

reviews.title: Many defects!!
reviews.text:
Subpar!!
Incomplete etymologies; inefficient and clumsy multiple definition entry search system (how would I know which definition I’m searching for before I know the meaning of the word??); few example sentences; very few recently coined or informal or idiomatic terms/phrases; and lastly, some inexplicable non-existence of common words, i.e. today I tried to look up the word “widow“ and it wasn’t there!

reviews.title: Be A Word Smith
reviews.text: If you a writer or student in High School or College consider downloading The Oxford Dictionary And Thesaurus. It is available in British and American English and in a wide selection of foreign languages. No other dictionary is as complete as an Oxford dictionary Dictionary. Included under word listing is word origin, pronunciation, variant meanings, synonyms and antonyms. There is also a daily word to help enhance vocabulary. Get it today! You can thank me later!

reviews.title: Ads even with subscription, lacking definitions
reviews.text: I was very disappointed in this app. Even with the subscription there were ads I had to wait for every time before searching for a word. Also, about a third of the words I searched using the app did not show up accurate or helpful definitions and I ended up googling the definition (where I did find correct ones). And these weren’t crazy words—they were ones I came across reading Charles Dickens, a pretty standard author for English lit classes.
